name: ServiceM8
summary: Job management for trades and service contractors: scheduling, quotes, job cards and invoicing.
best_for: trades and service businesses with a crew, where per-user pricing elsewhere punishes you for having enough people — this is one of the few tools in the category that does not
skip_if: you are a sole trader doing a handful of jobs a month — the free tier covers that, and at low job volume the paid tiers are buying capacity rather than features
honest_knock: Unlimited users on every paid tier is genuinely unusual in this category and worth saying first: put your whole crew in without the bill moving. The meter is jobs instead, and jobs are the thing you least control. Fifty a month on Starter is roughly two a working day, which a two-van operation passes in a busy month — and the next step is not a small one, it is $29 to $79. Count your jobs in your best month rather than your average, because that is the month that will bump you, and a seasonal trade will spend part of the year paying for a tier it does not need. The free tier at 30 jobs and one user is a real trial, not a plan.

plans.includes: 1 user, 30 jobs a month, SMS at 10c each

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-19 on their own pricing page, USD) Priced by jobs per month, with unlimited users on every paid tier. Free $0: 1 user, 30 jobs a month, SMS at 10c each. Starter $29: unlimited users, 50 jobs. Growing $79: 150 jobs. Premium $149: 500 jobs. Premium Plus $349: 1,500+ jobs, with additional jobs at 20c each — the only tier where the page prices an overage. Text messaging is listed as free on all four paid tiers, but the FAQ states there is an overage fee per SMS above each plan's monthly SMS cap, and neither the caps nor that fee are printed. Going over the job ceiling is not a hard stop: the FAQ gives seven further days of normal use, after which you either reach your monthly reset or are prompted to upgrade. A 14-day free trial with full feature access is offered and needs no card; there are no lock-ins and changes are pro-rata. The AI Smart Helper is listed as available on All Plans and the page prints no daily usage cap for it (our August reading recorded ten uses a day on Free; that limit no longer appears on this page). The full app is iOS; Android is served by the cut-down ServiceM8 Lite.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 30 October 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We went through the setup wizard, created two made-up quote jobs for two new clients and looked for an export.
findings: The trial runs 14 days with no card. The four-step setup asks for your industry, accounting software and branding, and the last two steps can be skipped.
New accounts include a sample job, and in our account its address was a real street near the location of the signup.
Client names lost their accents: 'TEST Zoë Alpha' became 'TEST Zoe Alpha' as soon as we created the client. The job description kept accents and line breaks.
A new job saves the moment you open it, with Quote as the default status.
We found no export for jobs or clients in the web app. Clients can be bulk-imported, and the reports are dashboards with totals.
not_tested: Support's answer (we emailed our three questions on 30 October)
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
